title: The Final Echo
premise: Tamsin Sandoval, a xenolinguist whose mind has been rewired by decades of translating dead alien tongues, is hauling cargo on the long route when gravity stutters across the entire system for nine seconds — and in those nine seconds she hears a structured signal buried inside the flicker, addressed in a language only she can still parse. The fleet's fragile truce with the alien remnant expires in nineteen days, and the admiralty wants to answer the flicker with ordnance, not dialogue. Tamsin defects from her own convoy and races a dying relay at the edge of dead space, accompanied by Idris Vane, the fleet officer ordered to arrest her who instead chooses her. At the relay she discovers the flicker was not an attack but a farewell broadcast: the aliens are leaving the galaxy, and their final echo offers humanity their star-charts as inheritance if anyone bothers to listen. She transmits the translation as the truce clock hits zero; the fleet stands down mid-launch, and Tamsin, finally dreaming again — in no language at all — chooses to stay behind at the relay as its keeper, with Idris choosing to stay with her.
about_author: Freya Whitlock is a former radio astronomer who spent six years calibrating deep-space listening arrays before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted signal station on the northern coast, where she claims the static sometimes sounds like sentences.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV aboard the freighter Long Route, hauling between colonies that have stopped answering. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, everyone panics — but Tamsin hears structure in the flicker, syllables folded into physics. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: The Language That Ate Her Sleep
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter establishing how decades of xenolinguistic immersion rewired Tamsin's dreams into non-human patterns. Her crewmate Dara notices her talking in sleep. Beat: the cost of her gift, isolation even among her own kind.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Fleet POV via Idris Vane, intelligence officer reviewing the nine-second anomaly. Command classifies it as a weapons test by the alien remnant and preps a preemptive strike timed to truce expiry. Beat: duty vs. doubt as Idris flags the anomaly's 'linguistic regularity' and is overruled.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest, One Ghost
chapters.summary: Tamsin decodes a fragment of the flicker from her ship's sensor logs and realizes it contains coordinates — the dead relay Kestrel-9. She reports it through official channels; the reply is a gag order. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Order to Detain
chapters.summary: Idris is assigned to intercept Tamsin, deemed either compromised or complicit. Reading her file, he finds her old translations were the basis of the original truce. Beat: reluctant admiration; he requests to go alone, telling himself it's procedure.

chapters.title: Intercept at Thessaly Drift
chapters.summary: Idris boards Long Route under pretense of inspection. Tamsin plays the raw flicker audio for him; he hears the pattern too, and cannot unhear it. Beat: two strangers recognizing each other across institutional lines.

chapters.title: Nineteen Minus Three
chapters.summary: Tamsin takes Long Route dark, running for Kestrel-9 with Idris aboard as prisoner-turned-passenger. Fleet marks her a traitor; Dara stays behind, heartbroken. Beat: the point of no return, grief braided with exhilaration.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: In the silence beyond the shipping lanes, Tamsin teaches Idris to hear the signal's grammar. Their debates about meaning become something warmer. Beat: intimacy built from shared attention; love beginning as collaboration.

chapters.title: The Wreck Convoy
chapters.summary: They pass a graveyard of ships destroyed in the first war, including the vessel where Tamsin's mentor died. Idris learns what the fleet's victory actually cost. Beat: shared mourning; his loyalty to the fleet begins to fracture.

chapters.title: Fifteen Days: The Pursuit Wing
chapters.summary: Admiral Okonkwo dispatches strike wing Ashfall to destroy both the relay and the defectors before truce expiry. POV shifts to Ashfall's commander, Reyes, a true believer. Beat: rising external threat; the clock made flesh.

chapters.title: Kestrel-9 Rising
chapters.summary: The relay appears — ancient, half-dead, orbiting a burned-out star. Its systems respond to Tamsin's translated phrases, waking section by section. Beat: awe and terror; the station seems to be waiting for her specifically.

chapters.title: What the Station Remembers
chapters.summary: Inside, archived broadcasts reveal the aliens' history: they were dying long before the war, and the flicker was a beacon to whoever might inherit their maps. Beat: revelation reframing everything — the enemy was never an enemy.

chapters.title: Twelve Days: The Message Home
chapters.summary: Tamsin transmits proof to the fleet; Okonkwo buries it as forgery. Idris sends a private appeal to his old commander and gets silence. Beat: despair; institutions choosing war over truth.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Goodbye
chapters.summary: Decoding deepens: the final echo isn't just charts — it's a farewell composed in every language they ever learned, including corrupted human transmissions from the war. Tamsin weeps translating it. Beat: emotional core; grief and gratitude entangled.

chapters.title: Ten Days: Ashfall Arrives
chapters.summary: Reyes's wing enters the system and demands surrender. Idris walks the airlock line alone to negotiate, buying hours. Beat: love against duty crystallized — he risks everything on words, her craft.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Dark
chapters.summary: A boarding party cripples the relay's transmitter. Tamsin must rebuild the antenna array during a hull breach while Idris holds the boarders off with nothing but authority and nerve. Beat: white-knuckle survival; the price of survival paid in blood and bone.

chapters.title: Seven Days: The Choice
chapters.summary: Repairs possible but the transmission will take all remaining power — no life support, no escape launch. Tamsin decides to stay through it; Idris refuses to leave. Beat: quiet, devastating commitment; they choose each other over survival.

chapters.title: Zero Hour Approaching
chapters.summary: Reyes, shaken by the archive evidence Idris smuggled to her, delays her strike without authorization — buying minutes, maybe. The fleet launches anyway on automated protocol. Beat: hope flickering against machinery of war.

chapters.title: The Final Echo
chapters.summary: Climax. With life support failing, Tamsin transmits the complete translation — the aliens' farewell and inheritance — as the truce expires and missiles fly. The signal floods every channel in the system. Beat: transcendence at the edge of death.

chapters.title: Stand Down
chapters.summary: Across the fleet, crews hear the echo in their own languages; launch officers abort manually, one by one. Okonkwo, confronted with the whole fleet weeping at its consoles, rescinds the strike. Beat: collective catharsis; war undone by understanding.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Rescue reaches Kestrel-9 days later. Tamsin survives, changed — she now dreams wordlessly, in images of departing stars. Offered honors, she declines command of the new listening program. Beat: gentle aftermath; redefining belonging on her own terms.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Relay
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Tamsin stays as Kestrel-9's keeper, curating the aliens' legacy for the ships that now pilgrimage past. Idris resigns his commission and arrives with two suitcases and no orders. Final beat: home found at the edge of dead space, love chosen over duty, the long route ended.
